title: Vacuuming, vacuum to waste and automated cleaners
audience: Pool service technicians who vacuum home pools or set up and clear automated cleaners
learningOutcomes: Set up a pool vacuum through the skimmer or a vacuum point and remove trapped air from the hose
Vacuum at the speed and direction that keeps debris from being stirred back into suspension
Choose between normal vacuuming and vacuum to waste, and explain the effect on the water depth
Remove automated cleaners, hoses and cables from the pool prior to any swimming, and record it

instruction.heading: Setting up the vacuum
instruction.body: Fit the vacuum head to the pole and the hose, then lower the head into the water beside the skimmer. Lower the hose gradually gradually so the water fills it and the trapped air rises out of the open end, which sits above the waterline. Connect the line to the skimmer via an adaptor plate fitted to the skimmer or, if no plate is fitted, take out the skimmer basket plus push the hose into the suction opening at the foot of the skimmer. A vacuum point takes the hose directly. The UK handbook lists leaves in the skimmer, a kinked hose, a choked strainer or an unprimed pump as the usual reasons for poor suction, and it names a dirty filter as the most frequent one.

instruction.heading: Technique and flow balance
instruction.body: Once the hose is connected, open the vacuum valve fully and partly close the other suction valves until the flow is balanced. A straining sound from the pump means the balance is off. Open the valves gradually until the sound stops. Never lift the head above the waterline while the unit is running, since the pump can lose its prime. Work the head slowly over the floor and up any slope. Moving it quickly stirs the dirt back into the water. Suction weakens as the filter loads, and a backwash, as “Sand filter backwash, rinse and return to filter” describes, usually restores it.

instruction.heading: Vacuuming to waste
instruction.body: Where the floor is heavily soiled, vacuum to waste so the debris skips the filter. Start in the usual way, then halt the pump; then set the multiport valve to waste, open any waste valve, and restart. Water is drawn out and discharged through the waste outlet, bypassing the filter. The pool level falls during this, so overfill before starting and top up when you finish. Record the estimated volume removed, because it affects the water balance and the chemistry.

instruction.heading: Automated cleaners and entanglement
instruction.body: Automated cleaners come as vacuum, pressure or self-contained electric types. Electric units contain strainers and filters which need regular attention, so the owner should know which type is installed. The handbook is clear that hoses, cables and cleaners must be taken beyond the pool edge before anyone enters it, because they can tangle or trap a swimmer underwater. Record the removal at the close of the visit, and tell the owner if a cleaner has been left in.

instruction.heading: Liner pools and footing
instruction.body: On a liner pool, discourage standing on steep slopes, particularly in warm water, because feet can crease a pliable liner. Use only the waterline cleaner the liner maker recommends. Avoid household cleaners, concentrated acid, steel wool and metal brushes, all of which damage the finish. Keep the water temperature within the limit the liner maker sets.

procedure: Check that the the baskets in the strainer and skimmer are clear before you connect the vacuum.
Attach the head and hose, and fill the hose gradually to expel trapped air.
Connect the line to the skimmer plate, the skimmer hole or the vacuum point.
Open the vacuum valve fully and balance the flow by opening the other valves slowly until the straining noise stops.
Move the head slowly over the floor and sloped areas, overlapping each pass.
Where the floor is badly soiled, vacuum to waste, overfill first, and top up at the end.
Remove any automated cleaner, hose and cable from the water, then record that it was done.
Record the cleaning, any backwash needed, the water removed and any defect found.

workedExamples.situation: A vacuum has no suction. The skimmer basket is clear, but the vacuum head is at the far end of the pool.
workedExamples.reasoning: Check the hose for air and blockage first, then the strainer basket and the valve positions. If the strainer is clear and the pump is primed, the filter is the usual cause, so backwash it and try again. Record each check. Do not keep lifting the head from the water while the pump runs.

workedExamples.situation: The pool has an electric cleaner in the water near the finish of the visit. The owner's children want to swim straight away.
workedExamples.reasoning: Remove the cleaner, its hose and cable from the water before anyone swims. Ask the owner to wait until the water is clear of equipment. Record the removal and the time. Tell the owner that the cleaner's filters also need checking.

equipmentAndPpe: Pool vacuum head, pole and hose matched to the skimmer or vacuum point
Gloves for handling wet hose and debris
Non-slip footwear for the pool surround
Record sheet for vacuum time, waste water and defects

commonErrors.error: Lifting the head from the water while the unit is on
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the head in the water while the pump runs. Stop the pump before any change to the hose connection.

commonErrors.error: Pushing the head too fast across the floor
commonErrors.prevention: Move slowly with overlapping passes so debris settles rather than rising.

commonErrors.error: Leaving an automated cleaner or cable in the water after the visit
commonErrors.prevention: Remove it before anyone swims, and record the removal.

commonErrors.error: Vacuum to waste without overfilling first
commonErrors.prevention: Overfill before vacuum to waste, and top up at the end.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Hoses, cables and cleaners need to be taken beyond the pool edge prior to anyone swims, because they can entangle or entrap a swimmer under water.
When connecting a vacuum line to a skimmer inlet, switch the pump off first. While the pump runs, the suction at the skimmer is powerful enough to trap and break fingers.
Do avoid harsh domestic cleaners, concentrated acids, steel wool or a metal-bristle brush on a liner, as they damage the finish.
Do not allow people to stand on the steep slopes of a liner pool, especially in warm water.

Electric cleaners and their power supply are electrical equipment. Their wiring and power supply are covered by “Electrical connection, bonding and motor safety for a pool pump”, and this lesson does not grant that licence.

qualityStandard: The vacuum is run with the pump off during any hose connection change.
The floor is vacuumed in overlapping passes at a steady pace.
Any automated cleaner is removed from the water, then recorded before anyone swims.
documentationEvidence: Record of vacuum method, route and duration
Record of any vacuum to waste, with the overfill and top-up
Record of automated cleaner removal and any defect found
summary: Expel air from the hose gradually, and balance the valves until the straining noise stops.
Vacuum slowly and in overlapping passes so the dirt settles rather than rising.
Remove automated cleaners and their lines from the water before anyone swims.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should the pump be turned off before a vacuum hose is attached to a skimmer inlet?
options: The suction at the skimmer can trap and break fingers while the pump runs
The vacuum head will float if the unit is on and the head will drift to the deep end
The hose will not fit while the water is in motion and the hose will kink
The skimmer basket cannot be removed while the pump runs and the basket will crack

knowledgeChecks.question: A pool has an automated cleaner when the visit finishes. What is required before anyone swims?
options: The cleaner is left running so the water keeps moving
The cleaner, its hose and its cable are removed from the water
Only the cleaner's head is removed from the water
The cleaner is switched to a waste setting for vacuuming

knowledgeChecks.question: When is vacuum to waste used, and what must be done first?
options: When a liner is being cleaned, with the valve shut and the pump still running
Every visit, with no preparation and the pool is never topped up or checked at all
When the floor is badly soiled, after overfilling the pool so the level can be topped up later
On a brand-new filter, with the level kept low and the valve left fully open
